native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Across the supplied meta-replication data, the original papers in the Experimental Economics project (project='ee') are on average ~28.0 pages long (mean=28.0, SD=7.4; n=18 rows, all unique originals; median=27.5; range 16–45), whereas the original papers in the Psychology replication project (project='rpp') are on average ~11.2 pages long (row-level mean=11.2, SD=6.3; n=97 rows / 95 unique originals; median=9.0; range 1–31; deduplicated-by-original-paper mean=11.2). Experimental Economics originals are therefore roughly 2.5× longer — about 16.8 more pages per paper — than Psychology originals in this dataset. The gap is robust to handling duplicates (only 2 duplicate originals exist, both within rpp, both carrying identical length values) and to the one flagged implausibly short record (rpp.53, length=1) which is retained per the no-silent-drop rule but does not change the rounded mean.
